newsitem.title: USA: Four Corners Ariz. power unit out a few days--APS.
newsitem.headline: Four Corners Ariz. power unit out a few days--APS.

text.p: A 750 megawatt coal-fired unit at the Four Corners power facility in Arizona will likely be down for a few days, Arizona Public Service Co (APS) said Wednesday.
APS, the unit's operator, said earlier Wednesday the unit likely would resume full power output at about noon, local time, today following a unexpected outage late Tuesday.
"It's going to take a few days. There were some problems with a bearing in a low-pressure turbine," said a company spokesman.
The company said earlier that the unit tripped off line about midnight when the power supply failed and the backup supply did not kick in.
The unit, number 5, was operating at full power when it tripped off line.
Power loads in the Southwest have been heavy this week, with temperatures hitting 102 degrees F on Tuesday and forecast to rise to above 100 F again today.
The June NYMEX Palo Verde electricity futures contract, with delivery at the Palo Verde, Ariz., nuclear power plant switchyard, was up 70 cents to $23.35 Megawatt hours as of 1304 EDT.
Traders blamed the move on the hot weather across most of the Desert Southwest.
